acceptanceCriteria: [integration] PermissionService.can(userPrincipal, 'project.read', { projectId: P }) returns { allowed: false, reason: 'not-granted' } when the user's rows are a ProjectMember ADMIN row in P and only a global member binding.

[integration] PermissionService.effectiveKeys({ type: 'AGENT', id }, { projectId: P }).has('ticket.create') returns false when the agent has an AgentProject row in P, an AgentRoleEntry DEVELOPER row and only a global agent binding.

[integration] PermissionService.effectiveKeys({ type: 'AGENT', id }, { projectId: P }).has('project.read') returns false for that same legacy-rostered DEVELOPER agent with only a global agent binding.
[integration] PermissionService.can(userPrincipal, 'project.read') with no project returns allowed: false when User.role is ADMIN and the user has only a global member binding.
[integration] PermissionService.can(userPrincipal, 'ticket.create', { projectId: P }) returns allowed: false for that same User.role ADMIN user with only a global member binding.
[integration] PermissionService.effectiveKeys({ type: 'USER', id }, 'global') returns the empty set when the user has no RoleBinding row at all.
[integration] PermissionService.can(userPrincipal, 'ticket.create', { projectId: P }) returns allowed: true when the user has a global admin binding and no project binding.

[unit] PermissionService built with three arguments (a role repository double, a binding repository double with only findEffectiveBindings and findAccessibleProjectIds, and a pass-through PermissionCache double) returns allowed: true from can(userPrincipal, 'agent.read') when findEffectiveBindings returns one global member binding whose permissions include agent.read, without calling any other repository method.
[integration] MembershipService.isGlobalAdmin(userId) returns false when User.role is ADMIN and the user has only a global member binding.
[integration] MembershipService.isGlobalAdmin(userId) returns true when the user has a global owner binding.

[integration] Given actor C holds global member and a custom GLOBAL role with ['user.update'], U1 is the only global owner/admin holder (global admin binding and User.role ADMIN), and U2 has User.role ADMIN with only global member, C's PATCH /admin/users/:id for U1 with { disabled: true } returns 409 users.lastAdmin.

[integration] Given the same actor C, no user holds a global owner/admin binding, and U2 has User.role ADMIN with only global member, C's PATCH /admin/users/:id for U2 with { disabled: true } returns 200 because U2 is not an admin and the last-admin guard does not apply.

[integration] PrismaUsersRepository.countActiveAdmins() returns 1 when one enabled user holds global admin, a disabled user holds global owner, and a third enabled user has User.role ADMIN without a binding.
[integration] PermissionService.effectiveKeys({ type: 'AGENT', id }, 'global') returns the empty set when the agent has no RoleBinding row at all.

routing.reasoning: Security-critical permission computation and last-admin protection change across services, persistence, cache/transaction regression fixtures and existing route tests; strict isolation is required.

'AC-7: legacy User.role ADMIN with no bindings grants user.create' (`newUser('ADMIN')` without a binding, expects `allowed: true`). The replacing invariant: that user is refused `user.create` with `not-granted`.

'the commit boundary of a nested write (B3)', it 'a nested demotion invalidates the permission cache only after the outer transaction commits', builds `newUser('ADMIN')` with no binding and expects `effectiveKeys(global)` to hold `user.create` before the commit; `PermissionService` is built with a fourth argument. AC-15 and AC-20 get their 200 from those bindings; AC-12 asserts that the update-roles route grants no key (the next ticket create of that agent stays 403); B2 removes the agent through the roster route and its warmed pickup is refused right after. AC-11, AC-14, AC-16 and AC-19 are unchanged.

'US-003 AC-11: a rostered VERIFIER-only agent picks up ...' gives the agent only an `AgentProject` row and an `AgentRoleEntry` `VERIFIER` row and expects pickup 200 and a `TICKET_SUGGESTED` event. The replacing invariant: the agent holds a `viewer` and a `verifier` binding in the project, and the pickup and event are unchanged.

'AC-5: a legacy ProjectMember DEVELOPER row keeps its access' expects 200 for a user whose only source is a `ProjectMember` row (seeded around line 166). The replacing invariant: that user gets 403 `projects` (a legacy row grants nothing).

userStories.title: Read membership and provenance from bindings only
userStories.description:
**Goal** — Replace the legacy membership query union and member chips/provenance with binding-only reads while preserving consumer call shapes.

**Motivation** — The schema feature cannot drop the legacy tables while anything reads them.

**Approach** — `apps/api/src/permissions/legacy-membership.queries.ts` is renamed `apps/api/src/permissions/membership.queries.ts` (and its spec `membership.queries.spec.ts`). Every legacy source is removed:
- **Sources** are now: a **project binding** of the principal in `P` (a `RoleBinding` with `projectId = P` whose role has scope `PROJECT`), and a **global project binding** (the same with `projectId` null, counted only in a live project). Local sources = project bindings; access sources = project bindings plus global project bindings. A GLOBAL-scope role's binding is still never a source.
- **Exports kept, with the same signatures:** `MEMBERSHIP_READ_CAP`, `userProjectRole`, `localProjectRole`, `agentHasProjectAccess`, `accessibleProjectIds`, `readAccessibleProjectIds`, `principalIdsWithAccess`, `listProjectMemberships`, `countActiveProjectAdmins`, and the `ProjectMembership` type re-export.
- **Removed:** `legacyRoleKeys` and its helpers (`userLegacyRoleKeys`, `agentLegacyRoleKeys`, `agentOnRoster`, `agentRoleEntryKeys`, `ROLE_KEY_BY_LEGACY_ROLE`, `ROLE_KEY_BY_AGENT_ROLE`), the legacy halves `legacyRowRole`, `legacyProjectIds`, `legacyPrincipalIds`, `legacyMembershipSources`, and `AGENT_ROSTER_ROLE` with the `ActorRole` import once nothing reads them. `principalIdsWithAccess` stays exported after US-004 and US-005 although no production code calls it then; its specs keep pinning it for drop-legacy-schema.
- **`ProjectMembership`** (`permissions.types.ts`): `since` is the earliest `createdAt` of the principal's project bindings in `P`; `addedByUserId` is that binding's `grantedById` when `grantedByType` is `'USER'`, else `null`. The doc comments stop naming legacy rows.
- **`countActiveProjectAdmins`** counts the distinct non-disabled users with a `project-admin` binding in the project.
- **`apps/api/src/projects/members/project-member.queries.ts`**: `readMemberBindings` returns only binding chips (no null-`id` legacy chip), and `readMemberRecord`'s `since` is the earliest project binding `createdAt`. The header comment stops describing the union, and helpers that only served the legacy chips are removed. The import moves to `membership.queries.ts`. `MemberBinding.id` keeps its type.
- **Importers** switch the module path and keep their calls: `email/email-content.builder.ts`, `home/prisma-home.repository.ts`, `notifications/ticket-mention.resolver.ts` (until US-005), `notifications/notification-eligibility.ts` (until US-005), `permissions/prisma-role-binding.repository.ts`, `agents/prisma-agent.repository.ts`, `projects/invites/prisma-project-invites-members.repository.ts`, `projects/members/prisma-project-members.repository.ts`, `projects/assignees/prisma-project-assignees.repository.ts` (until US-004), `projects/members/project-member.queries.ts`, `projects/prisma-project.repository.ts`, `tickets/prisma-tickets.repository.ts`. Doc comments in them that describe the legacy union are reworded.

Delivery notes: rename the existing integration query suite to membership-queries.integration.spec.ts and extend it with this story's ACs. Rewrite existing consumer tests and direct legacy roster/member fixtures as listed in this story's Modifies entries; retain negative legacy-only fixtures to prove they are inert. Legacy-only member PATCH becomes 404 members, while adding an agent whose only old row is AgentProject succeeds with 201. Preserve binding-only, read-cap, exhaustive keyset live-project listing and chip-paging behavior. Membership queries' existing error handling is unchanged; full capped reads warn and keep their first page, whereas exhausted safety-bound exhaustive scans still fail loudly instead of returning partial lists. Update any cap-constant imports added by US-001 too.

**Scope** — In: query module/spec rename, binding-only membership/provenance/chips, importers and affected fixture/test rewrites. Out: PermissionService computation/admin guard already delivered by US-001, scoping/auth principal/seed cleanup (US-003), replacing assignee access-source selection with key holders (US-004), replacing recipient/mention selection with effectiveKeys (US-005). Do not remove display role strings/legacy-project-roles.ts, legacy write/delete routes or tables, and do not change project/home lists into project.read-filtered lists.

**Interface** — The same exported function signatures are retained under membership.queries.ts, minus legacyRoleKeys. `ProjectMembership` remains the exported type with `since` and `addedByUserId` semantics above. Existing consumers continue passing the transaction-aware Prisma client as the first argument; this story introduces no public route or DTO contract changes.

[integration] userProjectRole(db, userId, P) returns null when the user's only source in P is a ProjectMember row.

userStories.title: Remove agent scoping and principal roles; bind the production seed
userStories.description:
**Goal** — Make agent project access unconditional on environment flags, remove legacy roles from authenticated agent principals, and give production-seeded admins real baseline/admin bindings.

**Motivation** — `AGENT_PROJECT_SCOPING=off` lets every agent into every project without any key, bypassing `project.read`.

**Approach** — No agent scoping switch, no agent roles on the principal:

| Site | Baseline (locate only) | Target |
|:--|:--|:--|
| `config/env.validation.ts` | `AGENT_PROJECT_SCOPING: Joi.string().valid('on', 'off').default('on')` | key removed; the schema keeps `.unknown(true)`, so a deployment that still sets it starts and ignores it |
| `config/auth.config.ts` | `agentProjectScoping?` in `IAuthConfig`, `AGENT_PROJECT_SCOPING_VALUES`, `IsOnOrOff`, `AuthConfigSchema.AGENT_PROJECT_SCOPING`, the factory field | all removed |
| `ProjectAccessService` | `(projectRepo, permissions, @Optional() @Inject(AUTH_CFG) authConfig?)`; `agentScopingEnabled()`; `resolveMembership` returns `null` for an agent when scoping is off | `(projectRepo, permissions)`; `agentScopingEnabled` deleted; every agent is decided by `can(principal, 'project.read', { projectId })` |
| `ProjectsService.findAllForPrincipal` | agent: `agentScopingEnabled() ? findAllForAgent(id) : findAll()` | agent: `findAllForAgent(id)`; the `readsEveryProject` branch first is unchanged |
| `AgentsService` | `agentScopingEnabled()`; `ProjectAgentListDto.from(records, this.agentScopingEnabled())` | method deleted; `ProjectAgentListDto.from(records, true)`. `AUTH_CFG` stays injected (`create` reads `apiKeySecret`), so the constructor is unchanged |
| `AgentPrincipal` (`auth/principal/koda-principal.types.ts`) | `agentRoles: readonly KodaAgentRole[]` | field removed; `KodaAgentRole` is deleted if nothing else imports it |
| `AgentAuthProvider.buildPrincipal` | loads `agentRoles`; `authorities: agentRoles` | loads only capabilities; `authorities: []`; `loadAgentRoles` deleted |
| `PrismaAuthRepository.findAgentRoles` | reads `AgentRoleEntry` | deleted |
| `AssistantToolExecutor` `agentPrincipal()` | `agentRoles: []` | field removed |
| comments naming the flag or the union | `tickets/tickets.service.ts` (`AGENT_PROJECT_SCOPING modes (D528)`), `permission.service.ts` (`projectIdsWithKey` doc), `agents.service.ts` (`suggestTicket` doc; the `updateRoles` comment that calls `AgentRoleEntry` a row the permission union reads), `project-access.service.ts` (the `resolveMembership` doc) | reworded |

### The production seed writes bindings (US-003)

`apps/api/prisma/seed.ts` keeps its env inputs (`KODA_ADMIN_EMAIL`, `KODA_ADMIN_PASSWORD`, `KODA_ADMIN_NAME`), its messages and the evaluation project, and moves the admin-user body into a new import-safe module, as `prisma/seed-e2e.ts` does with `prisma/seed-e2e-data.ts`:

```ts
// apps/api/prisma/seed-admin-data.ts
export type SeedAdminOutcome = { created: true; userId: string; roleKey: 'owner' | 'admin' } | { created: false };

/**
 * Creates the admin user when no user has `email`, with the global `member` baseline and a global
 * `owner` binding when no `owner` binding exists yet, else a global `admin` binding. An existing email
 * answers `{ created: false }` and writes nothing. The system roles are seeded first when missing.
 */
export async function seedAdminUser(db: PrismaClient, input: { email: string; name: string; password: string }): Promise<SeedAdminOutcome>
```

- It writes the bindings with `grantBaseline` and `grantRole` from `src/permissions/test-helpers/permission-fixtures.ts` (the helpers `seed-e2e-data.ts` already uses; `grantRole` seeds the system roles when a role row is missing and mirrors `User.role = 'ADMIN'` for `owner` / `admin`).
- The user row is created without a `role` field; the mirror sets it.
- Designer call: a seed run into an installation that already has an Owner binds `admin`, never a second Owner.

Delivery notes: preserve bcrypt hashing and script output, cache capabilities/status/blacklisting behavior, and ignored unknown-env behavior. userStories.description:
**Goal** — Add key-based principal enumeration and use it to drive user and agent assignee search.

**Motivation** — A custom project role without `project.read` is offered; a holder of a custom GLOBAL role with `project.read` is not.

**Approach** — Recipients and assignees by key (US-004, US-005):

`PermissionService` gains:

```ts
/**
 * The ids of the principals of `type` that hold `key` in the project, ascending and distinct.
 * Candidates are the principals with a binding that can apply there: a PROJECT-role binding in the
 * project or in every project, or a projectId-null binding of `owner`, `admin` or a GLOBAL role whose
 * entries expand to `key`. Each candidate is kept when `effectiveKeys(ref, { projectId })` has `key`.
 */
async principalIdsWithKey(type: PrincipalType, projectId: string, key: string): Promise<string[]>
```

- `PrismaRoleBindingRepository.findCandidatePrincipalIds(type, projectId, globalRoleIds)` returns the distinct `principalId`s of `type` whose binding has `projectId = P` (PROJECT role), `projectId` null with a PROJECT role, or `projectId` null with a role id in `globalRoleIds`, ascending, at most `MEMBERSHIP_READ_CAP` (a full read logs the cap warning, as the membership queries do).
- `globalRoleIds` are the GLOBAL roles (for example as read by `PrismaRoleRepository.findRolesByScope('GLOBAL')`) whose key is `owner` or `admin`, or whose `expandEntries(permissions, 'GLOBAL')` contains `key`. A role whose entries do not expand counts as not holding `key`.

Readers (`ProjectAssigneesService` in US-004; `NotificationEligibility` and `TicketMentionResolver` in US-005):

| Site | Baseline (locate only) | Target |
|:--|:--|:--|
| `NotificationEligibility.filter` | enabled users; a project draft passes for `role === 'ADMIN'` or `principalIdsWithAccess(projectId, 'USER')` | enabled users; a project draft passes when `(await this.permissions.effectiveKeys({ type: 'USER', id }, { projectId })).has('project.read')`, asked once per distinct (user, project); a draft with no project passes for any enabled user, as today |
| `NotificationEligibility.findGlobalAdminIds` | enabled users with `role: 'ADMIN'`, by `createdAt` ascending | the distinct enabled users with a `projectId`-null `owner` or `admin` binding (binding read capped at `MEMBERSHIP_READ_CAP`), by user `createdAt` ascending |
| `TicketMentionResolver.mentionedUserIds` | enabled mentioned users with `role === 'ADMIN'` or an access source | enabled mentioned users holding `project.read` in the project (`effectiveKeys`), in text order |
| `ProjectAssigneesService.search` → `PrismaProjectAssigneesRepository.search` | the repository reads `principalIdsWithAccess` for users and agents | the service asks `principalIdsWithKey('USER', projectId, 'project.read')` and `('AGENT', …)` and passes both id lists; the repository signature becomes `search(projectId, q, limit, ids: { userIds: string[]; agentIds: string[] })` and keeps its filters, order and limit |

- `NotificationEligibility` and `TicketMentionResolver` take `PermissionService` as their second constructor parameter, after `PrismaService`.
- `ProjectAssigneesService` takes `PermissionService` after its existing parameters.

Story ownership clarification: only the PermissionService/repository enumeration and ProjectAssigneesService/assignee repository row in that shared design are implemented here; the notification rows belong to US-005. Update projects/assignees/domain/project-assignee.domain.ts's search signature too. Retain existing disabled/status/query/order/limit/email-fallback mapping behavior and leave the ProjectMember CRUD base untouched. Remove assignee principalIdsWithAccess consumption, not the exported membership helper. DB reads or a candidate effectiveKeys rejection propagate unchanged without any partial answer. Invalid GLOBAL role entries are excluded from key candidates; computeKeys keeps its existing invalid-entry warning/no-grant behavior. A full candidate read answers its capped first rows and warns in the membership-query style. Do not generate 5,000-row integration fixtures.

Delivery notes: add project-read-assignees.integration.spec.ts and extend permission.service.spec.ts doubles/error cases. Service unit tests must pin USER/AGENT/key calls and the fourth ids argument, while repository tests accept ids directly and retain filter/order/limit assertions. HTTP ACs must prove the new enumeration is consumed by GET /projects/:slug/assignees, not only test the producer in isolation.

**Scope** — In: principalIdsWithKey, findCandidatePrincipalIds, service/repository/domain assignee-search seam and corresponding tests. **Interface** — `async principalIdsWithKey(type: PrincipalType, projectId: string, key: string): Promise<string[]>`. `PrismaRoleBindingRepository.findCandidatePrincipalIds(type, projectId, globalRoleIds)` has the candidate contract above. Assignee repository search becomes `search(projectId, q, limit, ids: { userIds: string[]; agentIds: string[] })`, with the existing return shape unchanged.

Consumers inject PermissionService without @Optional(); do not introduce module cycles or alternate authorization implementations. Respect repository/service/public layering and existing legacy direct-Prisma carve-outs (.nax/rules/api-data.md:20-86), generated Prisma imports, createPgAdapter and createTestPrismaClient. Binding reads belong in the existing repository or persistence-mapping queries, with bounded findMany calls. Its principal, project and role indexes already exist (apps/api/prisma/schema.prisma:1592-1607). The permission cache is generation-versioned with a 60-second TTL and tag invalidation; keep its behavior and transaction commit boundaries unchanged (apps/api/src/permissions/permission-cache.ts:10-41).
